lean.statement: ∀ {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {η : ℝ}, 0 < η → let J := MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun p : E × E => (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2)) (μ.prod (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)); ∃ R : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel E E, ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel R ∧ (∀ y, R y = μ.tilted (fun x => -‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η))) ∧ (J.map Prod.swap).IsCondKernel R
approved_definition_context: E has a real inner product inducing its norm and is finite dimensional. The given measurable space is exactly its Borel sigma algebra. IsProbabilityMeasure μ means μ has total mass one. μ.prod ν is the product measure; Measure.map f ρ is the pushforward law along f.

stdGaussian E is the centered Gaussian measure with identity covariance for the inner product, including the unique probability law in dimension zero. Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root. The scalar action • is real scalar multiplication, and Prod.swap sends (x,y) to (y,x).
Kernel E E assigns a measure to every input and requires the measure of each measurable output event to depend measurably on the input. IsMarkovKernel R means each measure R y has mass one.

For a real-valued f, μ.tilted f is μ.withDensity (x↦ENNReal.ofReal(exp(f(x))/∫exp(f) dμ)). The real integral is totalized when nonintegrable. No additional integrability premise is implicit in this definition.

For a joint measure ρ on E×E, ρ.IsCondKernel R means ρ.fst ⊗ₘ R=ρ, where ρ.fst is the first marginal and ⊗ₘ is measure–kernel composition-product. On a measurable rectangle A×B this composition has mass ∫⁻y∈A R(y,B) dρ.fst.
